source.title: ObscuraCoder: Powering Efficient Code LM Pre-Training Via Obfuscation Grounding
source.authors: Indraneil Paul; Hao Yang; Goran Glavaš; K. Kersting; I. Gurevych

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates downstream task scores across model sizes, a different measure from held-out cross-entropy scaling laws, and reports how performance trends vary by task and training regime.
record.gate_note: The paper mentions scaling laws as background but does not measure held-out pretraining loss, fit power laws, test extrapolation, or find compute-optimal parameter/token allocations. Its own size-scaling results concern downstream task performance.
record.test_reason: This is a pre-training-objective paper. It cites Kaplan and Hoffmann only as background and to justify corpus size, roughly an order of magnitude over Chinchilla-optimal. It fits no loss or scaling law and tests no extrapolation or allocation. Its 'RQ4 scaling' analysis (Fig. 2) plots ObscuraCoder's gain over a size-matched CausalLM against model size. That is the study's own method compared with a baseline, not downstream performance as a predictable function of scale. The absolute per-size scores in Tables 1–2 cover four sizes (255M–2.8B, about one order of magnitude). They come with no claim or test of predictability.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct, with one fix. The authors conclude that obfuscation-grounded pre-training improves code understanding, library-oriented generation, multilingual completion and summarization. Its gains over causal LM widen with model size, more so in zero-shot tasks than in fine-tuning. The 'scaling trends' they describe are trends in the method's gains, not in raw performance. They make no claim about scaling laws.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains code models with obfuscation-grounded objectives and evaluates downstream task performance across four sizes; it does not reproduce the original studies’ held-out-loss fitting or compute-optimal allocation methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported size-scaling trend differs by task regime: it is prominent in zero-shot evaluations and more modest, with saturation, in fine-tuning setups.

fits_no_version.finding: In Tables 1–2, absolute downstream scores rise monotonically across 255M, 491M, 1.2B and 2.8B for both CausalLM and ObscuraCoder. Examples: Multipl-E pass@1 for CausalLM goes 4.29, 5.84, 12.07, 16.70; BigCodeBench pass@25 goes 4.32 to 31.95. Defect-detection accuracy moves little (62.4 to 64.7). None of this is fitted or tested for predictability.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream code-task scores of small code LMs rise with parameter count at fixed 272B tokens, steeply for zero-shot generation and barely for fine-tuned classification.

fits_no_version.finding: The gain of obfuscation-grounded pre-training over causal LM widens with model size on zero-shot tasks (Fig. 2, Tables 1–3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The benefit of an auxiliary pre-training objective grows with model size.

record.problems: The size-scaling discussion is qualitative; Figure 2 supplies the plotted trends, but the text gives no fitted predictive relationship or uncertainty estimates for those trends.
record.rows_left_out: The paper’s Tables 1–3 report many per-checkpoint downstream scores, mostly for comparing training objectives or model families. The rows here capture the authors’ explicit size-scaling analysis in Section 5, RQ4 and Figure 2 rather than re-entering those task-comparison scores as scaling-law fits.

untested.parts: All: no held-out loss curves or power-law fits.
All: no extrapolation of fitted laws.
All: no compute-optimal allocation; Chinchilla is only cited to justify corpus size.
All: shapes vary with size, but no fixed-parameter comparison.
All: code pretraining with no loss scaling law fitted.
Predictability of downstream performance from scale or loss: no fit or prediction is made. Only four sizes have raw scores.

record.verdict_notes: The reader classified this as tests/T2 with a V6 'supports' label. That rests on misreading Figure 2, which shows gains over the baseline, not performance. Reclassified to cites_only/T6 and the V6 labels dropped. The raw per-size scores are noted under fits_no_version in case a researcher wants them.

rows.subject: ObscuraCoder suite
rows.operation_detail: Compared downstream performance across model sizes; the paper reports suite-level scaling trends.

conditions.value: zero-shot tasks, especially BigCodeBench library-oriented generation and Multipl-E multilingual generation

rows.measure: Downstream task performance as a function of model size
rows.baseline: Causal Code-LMs; exact figure values not stated in the text
rows.note: The authors describe scaling trends as prominent in zero-shot tasks, particularly library-oriented and multilingual generation; Figure 2 plots performance gains relative to causal Code-LMs.
rows.check: Figure 2 plots ObscuraCoder's downstream gain over CausalLM, not downstream performance versus size. The authors' 'scaling trends' describe how the method's benefit widens with size, which is a method-vs-baseline comparison, not V6. The baseline should read 'size-matched CausalLM'. No values are readable.

rows.subject: ObscuraCoder suite
rows.stage_stated: pre-trained; downstream fine-tuning for the evaluated fine-tuning tasks
rows.operation_detail: Compared downstream performance across model sizes; the paper reports suite-level scaling trends.

conditions.value: fine-tuning setups: CodeXGLUE defect detection and CommitChronicle

rows.measure: Downstream task performance as a function of model size
rows.baseline: Causal Code-LMs; exact figure values not stated in the text
rows.note: The authors report more modest gains from scaling in fine-tuning setups and describe saturation in fine-tuning performance, also noting saturation for a larger frontier model.
rows.check: This is the same Figure 2 gain-over-baseline measure, for the fine-tuning tasks. 'Saturation' refers to the method's gains, plus an aside about frontier models, which are cited comparisons. It does not bear on whether downstream performance scales predictably.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
